> **Session focus:** *ASCCR overview, POWER meeting structure, and reflective writing for professional growth*

## Learning Objectives

* Understand and apply ASCCR (Attitude, Structure, Content, Communication, Relationship)
* Use POWER to open, guide, and close consultations purposefully
* Develop reflective writing habits that drive skill improvement
* Practice openings that align expectations, scope, and next steps

## Description of Activities

On 19 May (Block 1), we introduced ASCCR, practiced the POWER structure for consultations, and grounded the day in reflective practice using structured frameworks (Gibbs, Kolb, Mezirow). Short role-plays emphasized intentional openings and shared outcomes.

## Reflection (Gibbs Reflective Cycle)

### 1. Description

We mapped ASCCR onto real consultations and practiced POWER (Purpose, Orientation, Work plan, Expectations, Review) to give meetings momentum and accountability. Reflection frameworks were positioned as tools to turn experience into growth, not just after‑the‑fact notes.

### 2. Feelings

I felt relief having a unifying scaffold—previous consultations felt improvised. POWER made openings easier and closings more decisive. Reflection felt familiar but more practical when treated as an iterative learning engine.

### 3. Evaluation

ASCCR helped me diagnose friction points (unclear roles, mismatched expectations). POWER translated those insights into concrete behaviors. Role‑plays surfaced micro‑skills (paraphrasing, timeboxing, agenda setting) I underuse. More feedback on tone and pacing would help.

### 4. Analysis

Short learning loops work: plan, act, reflect, refine. I’m replacing “jump to methods quickly shows competence” with “align on purpose and constraints first.” ASCCR also works as a diagnostic—if a conversation derails, I can ask which letter is weak.

### 5. Conclusion

Consultations improve when they are choreographed: purposeful openings, explicit scope, co‑authored next steps, deliberate closings. Reflection is part of practice, not separate from it.

### 6. Action Plan

I will use a one‑page POWER opener, an ASCCR checklist for debriefs, and 10‑minute post‑meeting notes (Gibbs prompts). I’ll ask collaborators for feedback on clarity of purpose and next steps to calibrate my delivery.
